holidays.name: International Museum Day
holidays.description: A day when museums around the globe celebrate their role in society, often with free admission, midnight openings, and quirky special exhibits. It's the perfect excuse to wander among dinosaur bones, ancient pottery, and suspiciously quiet security guards.
holidays.origin: Established in 1977 by the International Council of Museums (ICOM), with each year featuring a different theme.
holidays.funFact: Many museums take part in 'Museum Night' events around this date, where people can explore exhibits after dark, which is basically a real-life version of Night at the Museum.

holidays.name: No Dirty Dishes Day
holidays.description: A glorious unofficial holiday dedicated to avoiding the sink full of dirty dishes. Celebrate by using paper plates, ordering takeout, or eating directly from the pot like a delightful raccoon.
holidays.origin: An unofficial, fun-loving observance popularized through lists of quirky food and household holidays. Nobody knows who first declared it, but sink-haters everywhere approve.
holidays.funFact: The dishwasher was invented by Josephine Cochrane in 1886, reportedly because she was fed up with her servants chipping her fine china.

holidays.name: International Pickle Day
holidays.description: A tangy tribute to everything brined, fermented, and crunchy. Pickle fans snack on dills, gherkins, and even pickle-flavored treats like ice cream and candy.
holidays.origin: An informal food celebration created by pickle enthusiasts and food calendar compilers who believe cucumbers deserve a spa day in vinegar.
holidays.funFact: Cleopatra is said to have credited pickles for her beauty, and Americans eat billions of pickles every year.

holidays.name: Visit Your Relatives Day
holidays.description: A day devoted to dropping in on aunts, uncles, cousins, and that one relative who always asks about your love life. Bring snacks as a peace offering.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that encourages family bonding, listed among popular quirky holiday calendars as a reminder to reconnect with relatives you only see at weddings and funerals.
holidays.funFact: Studies on family connection suggest that regular contact with extended relatives is linked to better emotional well-being, so grandma's questionable casserole is actually good for you.

holidays.name: Endangered Species Day (Third Friday in May Observance Window)
holidays.description: A day for celebrating and learning about threatened plants and animals, from pandas to obscure beetles that deserve a fan club. Events often include wildlife walks, habitat cleanups, and adorable photo contests.
holidays.origin: Created by the U.S. Senate in 2006 to encourage people to protect endangered species and their habitats. It falls on the third Friday in May, so it sometimes lands near May 18.
holidays.funFact: The Endangered Species Act of 1973 has helped prevent the extinction of an estimated 99 percent of the species it protects, including the bald eagle.
